'''Satinder Vir Kessar''' (born 9 June 1932) is an Indian [[Synthetic organic chemistry|synthetic organic chemist]], academic and an Emeritus professor of [[Panjab University]].<ref name="Three PU professors make it to National Academy of Sciences">{{Cite news |title=Three PU professors make it to National Academy of Sciences |date=17 June 2015 |newspaper=Hindustan Times}}</ref> He is known for his researches in steroidal and [[heterocyclic chemistry]].<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N77-0368 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 October 2016}}</ref> He is an elected fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="TWAS fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/member/kessar-satinder-vir |title=TWAS fellow |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and all the three major Indian science academies, viz. The [[Indian National Science Academy]],<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N77-0368 |title=Indian fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Kessar,_Prof._Satinder_Vir |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]].<ref name="NASI Fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=K |title=NASI Fellows |date=2016 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=13 November 2016 |archive-date=15 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315081652/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=K |url-status=dead }}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1972, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | accessdate=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:StuC PU.jpg|thumb|235px|Student Centre, [[Panjab University]].]]
S. V. Kessar was born in [[Hoshiarpur]], in the undivided Punjab of [[British India]] on 9 June 1932 to Durga Dass, a lawyer and his homemaker wife, Susheela Devi.<ref name="Professor S. V. Kessar A Tribute ">{{Cite journal |last=Pandey |first=Ganesh |date=May 2002 |title=Professor S. V. Kessar A Tribute  |url=http://www.arkat-usa.org/get-file/19915/ |journal=Arkivoc |volume=VII |pages=1–7}}</ref> His schooling was at DAV Senior Secondary School, Hoshiarpur and later at [[Indian Military Academy]] after which he graduated in chemistry from [[Panjab University]] in 1953. While continuing his studies at the same institution for MSc by research,{{Refn|group=note|His adviser for master's degree was S. M. Mukherji}} he appeared for the [[Civil Services Examination]] in 1953 and stood among the top 100 candidates.<ref name="Central Services Examination">{{Cite web |url=http://www.pib.nic.in/archive/docs/DVD_39/ACC%20NO%20811-BR/HOM-1954-05-10_1173.pdf |title=Central Services Examination |date=1953 |publisher=Public Information Bureau, Government of India}}</ref> Choosing to pursue a career in chemistry, he passed MSc (hons) and moved to the US to join the [[University of Southern California]] where he studied under the guidance of M. C. Kloetzel to secure a PhD in 1958.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He stayed in the US for a while more to complete his post-doctoral studies at the laboratory of S. W. Benson and returned to India to start his career as an assistant professor at [[PEC University of Technology]] (then known as Punjab Engineering College). Returning to his alma mater, Panjab University in 1959 as a lecturer, he spent the rest of his academic career there where he served as a Reader (from 1963) and as a Professor (from 1974). On his superannuation from service, he was made the Emeritus Professor of the university. In between, he also served as a [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] Distinguished Chair from 1992 to 1997, the first professor to hold the position.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

Kessar is married to Urmi, his colleague at Panjab University and an art historian and they have two daughters, Bindu and Radha.<ref name="Professor S. V. Kessar A Tribute " /> The couple lives in Chandigarh.<ref name="NASI Fellows" />

== Legacy ==
Kessar's days with S. M. Mukherji during his master's degree research produced the first of his several articles, ''A Novel Synthesis of 4-Methyl-1 : 2-Benzanthracene'' which was published in [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] in 1954.<ref name="A Novel Synthesis of 4-Methyl-1 : 2-Benzanthracene">{{Cite journal |last1=Vig |first1=O. P. |last2=Kessar |first2=S. V. |last3=Mukherji |first3=S. M. |title=A Novel Synthesis of 4-Methyl-1 : 2-Benzanthracene |journal=Nature |date=October 1954 |volume=174 |issue=834 |pages=834 |doi=10.1038/174834a0|bibcode=1954Natur.174..834V |s2cid=4181618 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Later, he worked on the synthesis of [[pyrrolines]] which earned him his doctoral degree in 1958.<ref name="Heterocyclic Compounds. X. Hydrogenated Derivatives of Isoindole and 2-Azaazulene from Reductive Cyclization of γ-Nitro Ketones">{{Cite journal |last1=Kessar |first1=Satinder |last2=Kloetzal |first2=Milton C. |title=Heterocyclic Compounds. X. Hydrogenated Derivatives of Isoindole and 2-Azaazulene from Reductive Cyclization of γ-Nitro Ketones |journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry |date=1962 |volume=27 |issue=4 |pages=1314–1317 |doi=10.1021/jo01051a046}}</ref> Through his later day researches, he built the infrastructure of [[solanum]] alkaloids, accomplished the synthesis of [[azasteroids]] using a new pathway, and developed a protocol for linking aromatic rings which he utilized for the synthesis of the phenanthridine ring system and other heterocyclic systems as well as the synthesis of [[aporphine]] and related alkaloids.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | accessdate=5 October 2016 | pages=34}}</ref> Among the other natural products and drugs he synthesized include steroidal sapogenins, phenanthridine, aporphine, quinculidine, dextrorphan and venlafaxine.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He also elucidated the mechanistic pathways of the transformations and developed methodologies for benzyne cyclisation of anils and Lewis acid- promoted lithiation,<ref name="Lewis acid complexed heteroatom carbanions; a new concept for α-metallation of tertiary amines">{{Cite journal |author1=Satinder V. Kessar |author2=Paramjit Singh |author3=Rahul Vohra |author4=Nachhattar Pal Kaur |author5=Kamal Nain Singh |year=1991 |title=Lewis acid complexed heteroatom carbanions; a new concept for α-metallation of tertiary amines |journal=J. Chem. Soc., Chem. Commun.  |issue=8 |pages=568–570 |doi=10.1039/C39910000568}}</ref> both have since become standard synthetic procedures.<ref name="Satinder Vir Kessar on Neglected Science">{{Cite web |url=http://www.neglectedscience.com/alphabetical-list/k/satinder-vir-kessar |title=Satinder Vir Kessar on Neglected Science |date=2016 |publisher=Neglected Science}}</ref>

Kessar has authored several articles detailing his research findings which have been published in peer-reviewed journals.{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} He holds patent for one of the processes he has developed.<ref name="Patent">{{Cite web |url=https://patents.google.com/patent/WO2009118765A3/ja |title=Patent |date=2016 |publisher=Google Patents}}</ref> He served the executive council of Panjab University Alumni Association during 2014–15<ref name="Panjab University Alumni Association">{{Cite web |url=http://iqac.puchd.ac.in/docs/2014/20141027095354-annexure-n-alumni-council.pdf |title=Panjab University Alumni Association |date=2016 |publisher=Panjab University Alumni Association}}</ref> and has written a book on the city of [[Jaisalmer]].<ref name="Professor S. V. Kessar A Tribute " /> He also serves a member of the councils of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="Six Chandigarh Region Innovation of Knowledge Cluster institutions faculty members selected as Members of NASI, India">{{Cite web |url=https://www.cityairnews.com/content/six-chandigarh-region-innovation-knowledge-cluster-institutions-faculty-members-selected-mem |title=Six Chandigarh Region Innovation of Knowledge Cluster institutions faculty members selected as Members of NASI, India |date=16 June 2015 |publisher=City Air News}}</ref> and the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA) and was the vice president of INSA Council during 1993–94.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

== Awards and honors ==
Besides being a National Fellow of the [[University Grants Commission of India]] (1976–78) and an elected fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]] (1998),<ref name="TWAS fellow" /> Kessar is an elected fellow of the National Academy of Sciences, India,(1996),<ref name="NASI Fellows" /> Indian National Science Academy (1977) and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (1975)<ref name="TWAS fellow" /> and an honorary fellow of the Punjab Academy of Sciences.<ref name="Honorary fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://paspatiala.com/honorary.html |title=Honorary fellows |date=2016 |publisher=Punjab Academy of Sciences |access-date=13 November 2016 |archive-date=24 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024113658/http://paspatiala.com/honorary.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1972.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | accessdate=7 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archivedate=12 September 2012 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> Madhya Pradesh Council of Science and Technology awarded him the Jawaharlal Nehru National Science Award in 1991<ref name="Jawaharlal Nehru National Science Award">{{Cite web |url=http://mpcost.nic.in/WriteReadData/UserFiles/file/NATIONAL-SCIENCE.pdf |title=Jawaharlal Nehru National Science Award |date=2016 |publisher=Madhya Pradesh Council of Science and Technology}}</ref> and he received the Golden Jubilee Commemoration Medal of the Indian National Science Academy in 1992;<ref name="Golden Jubilee Commemoration Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#910 |title=Golden Jubilee Commemoration Medal |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=13 November 2016 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#910 |url-status=dead }}</ref> INSA would honor him again in 1996 with the Meghnad Saha Medal.<ref name="Meghnad Saha Medal">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#abs |title=Meghnad Saha Medal |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=13 November 2016 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#abs |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Association Award of the [[Indian Science Congress]] reached him in 2008<ref>{{cite book|title=The Pearson Current Events Digest 2009|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aatFJFXjnggC&pg=PA94|publisher=Pearson Education India|isbn=978-81-317-2723-2|pages=94–}}</ref> as well as the Lifetime Achievement Award of the [[Indian Chemical Society]] and he has delivered the Basudev Banerjee Memorial Lecture of the society. He is also a recipient of the Prem Singh Medal, Gold Medal of [[Chemical Research Society of India]], Hari Om Award and the Goyal Prize of the [[Kurukshetra University]].<ref name="Goyal Prize">{{Cite web |url=http://kuk.ac.in/userfiles/file/news/goyal%20prize%202008.pdf |title=Goyal Prize |date=2016 |publisher=Kurukshetra University}}</ref> [[Arkivoc]] journal issued a [[festschrift]] on Kessar in 2005 on his 70th anniversary year by way of its December issue.<ref name="Commemorative Issue in Honor of Prof. Satinde V. Kessar on the occasion of his 70th anniversary">{{Cite journal |title=Commemorative Issue in Honor of Prof. Satinde V. Kessar on the occasion of his 70th anniversary |url=http://quod.lib.umich.edu/a/ark/5550190.0003.701?rgn=main;view=fulltext |journal=Arkivoc |date=December 2005 |volume=2002 |issue=7}}</ref>
